newsitem.title: USA: CommEd to meet with nuclear regulators.
newsitem.headline: CommEd to meet with nuclear regulators.

text.p: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission said Wednesday it will meet May 14 with Commonwealth Edison Co to discuss apparent violations of NRC fire protection requirements at its Braidwood nuclear power station in Braidwood, Ill.

The enforcement conference will review apparent fire protection violations which were initially identified by the utility in mid-1996, the NRC said in a statement. They include roll-up doors which did not meet a specified three-hour rating as fire doors and several instances of inadequate separating of electrical cables in parallel portions of safety systems.

The decison to hold an enforcement conference does not mean that the NRC has determined that a violation has occurred or that enforcement action will be taken, it said. The purpose is to discuss apparent violations, their causes and safety significance, and to allow the company to outline its proposed corrective actions, the NRC said.
No decisions or enforcement action, such as a fine, will be made at this conference. Those decisions will be made by senior NRC officials at a later date, the NRC said.
Commonwealth Edison is a subsidiary of Unicom Corp.
